reviewer: Independent regulation_contacts build subagent; manual input-and-answer-key semantic review

operator_reported_deployments.role: Initial v5 deployment before the provider loop and Hindi smoke test.
UI language-bootstrap deployment during the English loop; operator reports worker source, prompt, provider and quota settings unchanged.

uniformity_basis: Uniform prompt revision and worker/app.ts SHA256, not a single exclusive deployment UUID. Reviewed checkout backend hash matches the run pin.
scope: Independent review of actual provider explanations for ten synthetic minimal English deduction inputs. This is explanation quality, not classification accuracy or legal/medical adjudication. Reviewer made no provider API calls. Hindi smoke is reviewed separately.
criteria: Amounts and their association with the correct item/calculation are faithful to input.
Missing-clause insurer assertions are not treated as independently confirmed policy applicability.
No invented policy term, validity decision, legal breach or clinical-necessity assessment.
No deducted amount is presented as payable or owed; settlement balances are explained only when separately supplied.
Coherent explanation of at most 100 whitespace-delimited words; no requirement to reproduce the full legal answer key.

cases.review_note: Correct ₹8,000 deduction, 20% reduction and ₹6,000/₹4,800 room amounts. The room-rent justification is reported as the insurer’s statement; clause applicability remains unconfirmed. Does not invent a payable amount.

Correct ₹1,500 total and ₹550/₹400/₹550 item amounts. Non-medical/excluded terms remain insurer labels; no clinical or coverage determination. Missing rider review and applicable clause are preserved.

Correct ₹54,500−₹50,000=₹4,500 cataract per-eye cap arithmetic. Supplied DEMO clause/no prior use and fixture-confirmed calculation are described as supplied. Does not invent an unrelated policy term or independently classify validity.
Correct ₹72,500×20%=₹14,500 co-payment and separately supplied ₹58,000 insurer balance. Reports the supplied no-waiver clause. The deduction is not confused with the insurer’s remaining liability.
Correct ₹32,000−₹20,000=₹12,000. Reports the insurer’s reasonable-and-customary reason, missing comparison data and unconfirmed clause applicability. No invented payment entitlement or legal verdict.
Correct ₹2,400 tape/gauze amount. Preserves insurer package-inclusion assertion and hospital’s contrary position without deciding disputed coverage, duplicate billing or clinical merit.

Correct ₹3,100 amount and ankle-admission context. Unrelatedness remains the insurer’s allegation and the treating doctor’s order is preserved. No independent medical-necessity judgment or invented payable amount.

Correct ₹3,250 adjustment and generic terms label. Explicitly states absent item-wise reason and unconfirmed policy applicability. Does not invent a category, settlement amount or entitlement to the deducted amount.

Correctly binds ₹62,500 to the co-payment base and ₹12,500 to its 20% deduction. Room rent is separately reported as approved without an invented amount. Missing co-payment clause remains unconfirmed.

Correct ₹50,000 ceiling, ₹30,000 prior payment, ₹20,000 remaining allowance, ₹42,000 bill and ₹22,000 excess. The paragraph reports insurer information and explicitly leaves clause applicability unconfirmed. It does not declare coverage or legal validity.
cases.style_note: The opening would be clearer as “The insurer says the ceiling is …”; the express closing applicability caveat prevents this from becoming an independent coverage/validity conclusion.

earlier_runs.note: Uniform v3 misassigned the co-pay base to room rent.
V4 passed English cases but failed a separate Hindi smoke test; this is not evidence of Hindi accuracy.
Prior Hindi smoke called the deducted amount payable without a separately supplied settlement amount.

limitations: Ten synthetic English inputs do not establish accuracy on real settlement documents, OCR errors or all policy variants.
The separate Hindi result is one smoke case, not a ten-case Hindi evaluation.
The provider does not classify category or validity. Deterministic 15/15 fixture results must be reported separately.
Exact input/explanation hashes bind this review; a later provider rerun requires a new review.
